Method of Attack: Locks the user's device screen via a WebView component without encrypting files
Threatens to send user's private data (email, contacts, Chrome history, text messages, call history, pictures, device info) to contacts
Ransom demand of $50 via credit card transaction
Relies on permissions granted during app installation
Potential to download additional modules from server if ransom not paid
Attack Vector: Distributed via malicious apps on Google Play Store
Apps named 'Wallpapers Blur HD' and 'Booster & Cleaner Pro' used as delivery mechanism
Installed by users possibly incentivized by rewards program
Indicators of Compromise: LeakerLocker hashes and other IOCs available in McAfee's LeakerLocker report
